class.name: PathInfo
class.brief_description: All forms and facts of one path, as resolved by [PathPrefixServer].

method.name: exists
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if a file or a folder exists at this path. This touches the file system. Returns [code]false[/code] if the path is not [member valid].

method.name: is_dir
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if a folder exists at this path. This touches the file system. Returns [code]false[/code] if the path is not [member valid].

members.member: [code]true[/code] if the prefix of the path works on this platform and in this build.
The folder of the path in its local form, for example [code]user://saves[/code] for [code]user://saves/a.json[/code]. Directly below a prefix this is the prefix itself.

[constant OK] if the path is [member valid], otherwise the reason: [constant ERR_FILE_BAD_PATH] for unknown prefixes, [code]..[/code] segments that leave the root, absolute paths in [method PathPrefixServer.resolve_safe] and paths outside the allowed roots; [constant ERR_UNAVAILABLE] for prefixes that do not work on this platform; [constant ERR_FILE_NO_PERMISSION] for read-only paths that were requested for writing; [constant ERR_INVALID_PARAMETER] for an empty path.
A readable description of [member error]. Empty if the path is [member valid].
The extension of [member file_name] without the dot, for example [code]json[/code].
The last segment of the path, for example [code]a.json[/code].

The path in the file system of the OS, with [code]/[/code] as separator. Empty where there is no such path, for example for [code]res://[/code] files inside a PCK. [b]Note:[/b] On the Web, [code]user://[/code] maps to the in-browser file system ([code]/userfs/...[/code]), which is not a path on the user's disk.

The canonical prefixed form: the prefix in lowercase, [code]/[/code] as separator, [code].[/code] and [code]..[/code] resolved. Use it to compare paths and as a cache key. Empty for a global path that is not below any prefix.
[code]true[/code] if the prefix is one of the engine prefixes ([code]res://[/code], [code]user://[/code], [code]uid://[/code], [code]pipe://[/code], [code]exec://[/code]), which cannot be changed.
The canonical prefix, for example [code]user://[/code]. Empty for a global path that is not below any prefix.
[code]true[/code] if the prefix cannot be written to, for example [code]res://[/code] in an exported project.
The part after the prefix, for example [code]saves/a.json[/code].
The path exactly as it was given.
[code]true[/code] if the path was resolved. If [code]false[/code], see [member error] and [member error_message].
